q: Do net metering and open access solar projects have to use ALMM List-II solar cells?
title: ALMM List-II cells: net metering, open access
short: Yes, with a window. Net metering and open access solar projects commissioned from 1 June 2026 must use ALMM List-I modules and List-II cells, but MNRE's July 2026 memorandum lets them commission without List-II cells until 31 December 2026. Projects commissioned after that must comply.
audience: Factories installing rooftop or open access solar, and their EPC contractors

ul: MNRE's memoranda of 9 December 2024 and 28 July 2025: net metering and open access projects commissioned on or after 1 June 2026 must source modules from ALMM List-I and cells from ALMM List-II.
MNRE's memorandum of 18 July 2026: no blanket extension of List-II, but a limited window lets net metering and open access projects commission with exemption from List-II until 31 December 2026.
Before this, the dispensation for these projects ran until 31 May 2026.
Projects commissioned after 31 December 2026 must comply with List-II.

sections.h: What it means for a project now
ol: If commissioning will slip past 31 December 2026, specify List-II cells in the purchase order now.
Ask the EPC contractor for the module model, its ALMM List-I entry, and the cell manufacturer and model.
Keep the module datasheets and invoices; the discom may check them at net metering or open access approval.

p: ALMM List-II covers solar cells made by enlisted manufacturers at enlisted plants. A project that misses the window with non-listed cells risks delays in its net metering or open access approval.

senseible: Senseible can store your solar installation documents, module datasheets and commissioning certificate next to the generation readings, so the evidence for both compliance and Scope 2 sits in one record.
